CLAUDE.md — sharedimp (R)

Source: CLAUDE.md

What this package is

sharedimp implements the linear-regression variant of Ultra-marginal Feature Importance (UMFI-LR, Janssen, Guan & Robeva, AISTATS 2023) as a careful, resampling-based R package built on tidymodels (parsnip / rsample / yardstick). It is a companion to the Python package in ../sharedimp-py; both follow docs/specification.md, which is the single source of truth for the algorithm, inputs, outputs and metric conventions. Paper benchmarks live in ../sharedimp-experiments, not here. Never edit files in the sibling repositories from this one; report differences instead.

We do not claim a new importance measure. Do not describe the output as a causal or conditional effect. Do not add confidence intervals, p-values, or other formal inference. Keep the user-facing API small: shared_importance() plus a few accessors and low-level helpers.

Algorithm (summary; details in docs/specification.md)

For each anchor feature i and each resampling fold:

  1. On the training rows only, regress every other feature X_j on X_i (OLS with intercept) and keep (a_j, b_j).
  2. Residualize training and assessment rows with the same coefficients: R_j = X_j − a_j − b_j X_i.
  3. Full representation [X_i, R_{-i}]; reduced representation [R_{-i}] (residual columns constant on the training fold are dropped from both).
  4. Fit the learner on both representations, predict the assessment rows, evaluate the metric on each.
  5. importance = s * (metric_full − metric_reduced) with s = +1 for maximize metrics and −1 for minimize metrics, so positive always means “keeping the anchor helps”. Negatives are kept.
  6. Aggregate by the mean over folds; report fold-level results too.

Defaults: 5-fold CV (stratified for classification), random forest via ranger with 500 trees / min_n = 5, MSE for regression and multinomial log loss for classification.

Code layout

  • R/residualize.R — pure matrix core: residualize_fit(), residualize_apply(), build_representations(). No learner or tidymodels code here.
  • R/learners.R — learner adapters: sharedimp_learner(), built-in "linear" and "rand_forest", parsnip model_spec adapter, null model.
  • R/metrics.R — metric adapters around yardstick; direction handling.
  • R/shared_importance.R — orchestration (folds × anchors), seeding, errors.
  • R/result.R — sharedimp_result class, print(), fold_results().
  • R/direction.R — optional direction diagnostic.
  • tests/testthat/ — one file per concern; see “Testing”.
  • docs/specification.md — shared spec. docs/umfi_comparison.md — record of the numerical comparison with the reference implementation.

Development environment

R is not on the PATH on this machine. Use the conda environment:

R=/home/koki/anaconda3/envs/sharedimp-dev/bin/Rscript
$R -e 'devtools::document()'
$R -e 'devtools::test()'
$R -e 'devtools::check()'          # full R CMD check
$R -e 'devtools::build_vignettes()'

Run devtools::document() after changing roxygen comments; NAMESPACE and man/ are generated, do not hand-edit them.

Constraints

  • Numeric predictors only; no imputation; factors in x are an error.
  • Residualization coefficients must be estimated on the training fold only. Any change touching build_representations() must keep the leakage tests passing.
  • Fixed hyperparameters inside shared_importance(); no tuning.
  • Negative importance is never truncated.
  • Metric direction is taken from the yardstick direction attribute; never hard-code a sign for a named metric elsewhere.
  • Learner failures on a fold produce NA for that fold plus a warning, not an abort (unless on_error = "error").
  • Dependencies: Imports are parsnip, rsample, yardstick, ranger, rlang, tibble, stats. Everything else (glmnet, kernlab, ggplot2, …) is Suggests and must be guarded with requireNamespace().
  • Target CRAN quality: R CMD check with no ERRORs/WARNINGs; examples run in seconds; tests deterministic (always pass seed).

Testing policy

Start from tiny deterministic synthetic data and verify against hand computation before testing behaviour statistically.

  1. Residualization coefficients equal lm(X_j ~ X_i) on the training rows.
  2. Training and assessment rows are transformed with the same coefficients.
  3. Assessment rows do not influence the coefficients (perturbing assessment rows leaves training representations unchanged).
  4. Full / reduced representations have the specified columns and order.
  5. With the linear learner and MSE, importance matches the analytic expectation on a linear-Gaussian design.
  6. Exact duplicates and independent predictors behave as specified.
  7. Comparison with the reference UMFI-LR preprocessing (function vendored in the test under its MIT licence) — document, never fabricate, agreement.
  8. Smoke tests for regression / binary / multiclass with both built-in learners and a parsnip spec.
  9. Negative importance survives; learner failures yield NA + warning.

Use custom learners that record the matrices they receive to test the pipeline without depending on a particular model.

Commit discipline

Small, focused commits with imperative messages. Run devtools::test() before committing; run devtools::check() before pushing anything that changes DESCRIPTION, NAMESPACE, or exported functions. Never report a test or check as passing without having run it.
